#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR could be an alternative to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107734.

Currently, if we update a static pod multiple times while it restarts, the static pod can't start.

This PR 
- allows a podWorker to start if it is blocked by a pod that has been terminated before starting
- cleans up an undesired podWorker that does not start yet

issue_context.body:
### What happened?

In Kubernetes 1.23 we are seeing some static pods fail to start. These static pods failures are on quick remove and adds leaving the static pod not started.

We need to revert kubernetes/kubernetes#104743.

cc @gjkim42 

### What did you expect to happen?

All static pods should restart.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```diff
diff --git a/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers_test.go b/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers_test.go
index 4028c06c292..0e852594a40 100644
--- a/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers_test.go
+++ b/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers_test.go
@@ -880,3 +880,34 @@ func Test_allowPodStart(t *testing.T) {
 		})
 	}
 }
+
+func TestUpdatePodWithQuickAddRemoveStaticPod(t *testing.T) {
+	podWorkers, _ := createPodWorkers()
+	staticPodA := newStaticPod("0000-0000-0000", "running-static-pod")
+	staticPodB := newStaticPod("0000-0000-0000", "running-static-pod")
+
+	podWorkers.UpdatePod(UpdatePodOptions{
+		Pod:        staticPodA,
+		UpdateType: kubetypes.SyncPodCreate,
+	})
+
+	podWorkers.UpdatePod(UpdatePodOptions{
+		Pod:        staticPodA,
+		UpdateType: kubetypes.SyncPodKill,
+	})
+
+	drainAllWorkers(podWorkers)
+
+	podWorkers.UpdatePod(UpdatePodOptions{
+		Pod:        staticPodB,
+		UpdateType: kubetypes.SyncPodCreate,
+	})
+
+	drainAllWorkers(podWorkers)
+
+	t.Logf("rphillips waitingToStartStaticPodsByFullName=%v", podWorkers.waitingToStartStaticPodsByFullname)
+	if status, ok := podWorkers.podSyncStatuses["0000-0000-0000"]; ok {
+		t.Logf("rphillips podSyncStatuses=%+v", status)
+	}
+	t.Logf("rphillips startedStaticPodsByFullname=%v", podWorkers.startedStaticPodsByFullname)
+}
```

Not a super easy way to reproduce, I agree 😄 

Using this "method" I manage to reproduce several time with kubelet 1.22.5 and when I downgraded to 1.22.4 I didn't.

Thanks to @TeddyAndrieux. I can reproduce this bug quite easily.

1. Make a static pod not terminating within graceTreminationSeconds.
2. Change the static pod manifest with the same name (e.g. I simply change its `.spec.resources.requests.cpu`)
3. Change the static pod multiple times again ~while the static pod is terminating(updating)~ **_before it restarts(while there is no running static pod with the same full name)_**.

Then, the static pod with the same name never starts again.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
  containers:
  - args:
    - -c
    - trap "sleep inf" SIGINT SIGTERM SIGHUP &&  nc -k -l -p 4444
    command:
    - /bin/sh
    image: docker.io/library/busybox:latest
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: test
    ports:
    - name: test
      containerPort: 4444
      hostPort: 4444
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m # change it simply
        memory: 10Mi
```

The bug is still reproduced at master(after #107695)

/reopen

The problem is that terminating a static pod requests termination to podWorkers and removes the static pod from podManager.

When a static pod is waiting to start and termination requested, the static pod is enqueued to workQueue at podWorkers, but it cannot be re-requested again as it has been already removed from podManager.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2e68fd2857cded9cb470e3bf22ba01bb4934c6f8/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1877-L1899

Made a fix for this at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107854

Shouldn't this be 
```suggestion
				err = createStaticPodWithGracePeriod(podPath, staticPodName, ns,
```
? Otherwise we're not testing what we claim to test.

This function is only used to trigger multiple updates during the graceful termination period of a static pod(it doesn't matter if it has grace termination seconds or not).
The static pod we are updating already has grace termination seconds at BeforeEach stage.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/954fa57f0ead10b520328e1b936912290ced62ee/test/e2e_node/mirror_pod_grace_period_test.go#L40-L55
This condition block is confusing.  It really needs to be clearer.  Can you describe in a comment above the section what it's trying to do?  It's not clear to me why you are checking waiting here.

This condition block implies "if static pod" ...

I did it because there is only uid parameter in this function.
Do we have to add isStaticPod to podSyncStatus struct?
I'm asking "why do you need to process this here" - i.e. describe the problem this code block is trying to solve.

Ok, so you're trying to stop a worker during the cleanup phase.  Yes, this is definitely broken.

The core issue here is that the cleanup phase (syncing known pods) for an unstarted pod is not the same as when a worker itself completes.

I think the current approach may not be correct because this is the opposite flow from the normal worker termination (where the worker is who sets .finished).  Thinking about the problem, one sec.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107900/files#diff-c6d21f5481c391a3f32bcfddf45c9c20132b2876e8be9690289474b76b71d809R868 i think is going to be easier to deal with long run - the only thing that closes a loop is the loop itself.

You can't check pod fullname in this map unless this pod is a static pods.  So this needs to be inside an "if static pod" block.  Also my other comment with "I don't understand what this is trying to do" is complicating me reviewing this bit.
Will clarify and add comments.

This condition is not correct - we can't start the pod until it is fully and absolutely removed.  How did we end up with the pod still in this sync status?

Note that cleanup takes a significant period of time in some workloads, so with this change it could be tens of seconds after the pod finishes termination before it's fully cleaned up.  Is that being taken into account?

Ok, after looking at the e2e run I see the same thing as you.  The pod was added to waiting, then terminated, but the pod worker doesn't start because of the intervening updated pods.  If we see a pod here, it's never been started (because it is waiting), but if the waiting pod was marked deleted, we must purge it.

I like the cleanliness of keeping the logic here, but this does expose us to the potential of a large number of updates being kept (contiuously updated static pod would generate O(updates) worth of map entries, instead of O(1)).  Let me look a bit further at what we could do here.
I'd say we stay focused now without changing where this code lives - you can abuse kubelet worse simply by creating lots of pods.
Mabye we just leave a TODO here which is "This is O(N) with respect to number of updates to static pods with overlapping names, and ideally would be O(1)"
done

If you don't create a pod with a fixed UID, then every update is going to have to wait until the old pod is completely cleaned up before the new one is started (it's the same as waiting in the apiserver for the pod to be fully deleted before another one can be created).  This test doesn't seem to make sense to me - because the UID isn't static and so no mirror pod update is possible (the UID should be changed).

Although I may have incorrectly `checkMirrorPodRecreatedAndRunning` - which takes the UID and makes sure it is different.

If so, then this test does seem to be showing "updates to the same static pod name/namespace with different uids repeatedly don't converge".

> If so, then this test does seem to be showing "updates to the same static pod name/namespace with different uids repeatedly don't converge".

Yes, that is what I want to test here. Do we have to change its description? I think we don't want to describe "different uids" in this e2e test as it is the implementation detail.

Different UIDs is actually the bug here.  If the UID was the same, we wouldn't have this problem.  "A static pod that doesn't reuse a UID can't be updated repeatedly".  So I think it should be part of the description of the test
It would be good to add a value that checks the map after allowPodStart to verify we prune the results.  After this test, `foo_` should have `[uid-1]`
